_comment: capreq slug -> that capability requirement in Jama Connect. Two facts per
capability, and they do different jobs:
jama_key  the document key, e.g. PLAT3-PRD_Rqmts-4269. This is what the
trackers' Capability column now holds, so it is an ALIAS for the
capreq slug: load_capability_aliases turns it back into the slug
before anything groups, counts or renders. Without it every tile
degrades to a raw key and every row fails validation.
item_id   the numeric id in the Jama URL, e.g. 7466995. Substituted into
url_template to make the tile link. A complete URL may be given
instead and is used verbatim.
Either may be empty. An empty jama_key just means no tracker uses that key
yet; an empty item_id renders the tile unlinked. Both are named on stderr.
Replaces capability-jira.json, deleted 2026-09-05, when Jira Initiatives,
Objectives and Epics were designated for removal. ASI DevOps syncs Jama
'User Story' to Jira 'Story' for sprint boards, and the story-to-System-
Requirement relationship lives in Jama - so Jama is the only place the
capability layer still exists as an item.
All 15 capabilities are listed, not the 9 that had a Jira Initiative: Jama is
the requirements system of record, so every capreq exists there. Only 9 have
a jama_key because only 9 are referenced by a tracker today.
Hand-maintained INPUT, like tracker-schema.json - not a build product. It is
the one thing about a capability prak-v-model does not yet carry; cap_id,
title and priority all come from capreq frontmatter. Add `jama-id` there and
the reader prefers it, exactly as it did for jira-key - then delete this file.
